title: Quantitative Molecular Imaging using Deep Magnetic Resonance Fingerprinting
author: Nikita Vladimirov
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.pex-2612/v1
materials: Slowly insert the subject into the magnet.

steps.title: Prepare L-arginine Phantoms
steps.instruction: Create L-arginine phantoms for preliminary assessment of parameter quantification performance.

substeps.instruction: Weigh the required L-arginine powder (MW: 174.20 gr/mol) for the largest sample concentration (e.g., 100 mM) using a spatula, weighing paper, and balance, based on the volume of the intermediate container (e.g., 50 mL Falcon tube).
Add PBS 1x and stir thoroughly using a vortex mixer in a closed container; visually verify solubility.
Titrate the sample to desired pH levels (e.g., pH 4, 4.5, 5, 5.5, or 6 for L-arginine) using NaOH/HCl and a pH meter, stirring between measurements.
Pour the solution into 2 mL glass vials (preclinical) or 15 mL test tubes (clinical).
Synthesize additional samples via serial dilution using the remaining solution in the 50 mL Falcon tube and titrate to the desired pH.
Position three 2 mL glass vials (preclinical) in a new 50 mL Falcon tube, or six 15 mL test tubes (clinical) in a dedicated holder.
Fill the large phantom container completely with PBS 1x or saline, minimizing air bubbles.

steps.title: Install CEST-MRI Simulator
steps.instruction: Install the signal simulator from the molecular-mrf repository.

substeps.instruction: Download/clone the simulator from https://github.com/momentum-laboratory/molecular-mrf.
Ensure prerequisites are installed: C/C++11 compiler, SWIG, and Python v3.9 or newer.
Create and activate a clean Python v3.9 environment using conda or venv (e.g., 'conda create –n name_of_env python=3.9').
Navigate to the repository folder and install the simulator using 'pip install –e .'.
Verify installation by running 'pip list' to confirm BMCSimulator 0.2 and cest-mrf 0.2 are present.

steps.title: Load Pulse Sequences into MRI Scanner
steps.instruction: Install the required CEST-MRF pulse sequences onto the MRI hardware.

substeps.instruction: For preclinical (Bruker) scanners: Download the complete pulse sequence from https://osf.io/52bsg and install per the provided manual.
For clinical scanners (pulseq framework): Load .seq files into the scanner computer (typically c:\MedCom\Mricustomer\seq\pulseq\) as per the pulseq manual.
Obtain compound-specific pulse sequences from the 'supplementary/published_pulse_sequences/' folder in the molecular-mrf repository or the pulseq CEST open library.

steps.title: Create Custom CEST-MRF Pulse Sequences
steps.instruction: Define and build a custom MRF sequence (e.g., for L-arginine at 9.4T) using pypulseq.

substeps.instruction: Import pypulseq and define acquisition parameters (e.g., saturation pulse at 3.0 ppm, 30 images with varying B1 powers, pulse duration 3s, Trec 1s, B0 9.4T).
Define the readout: 60-degree flip angle block pulse (duration 2.1e-3), imaging delay (20e-3), and pseudo ADC (duration 1e-3).
Build the sequence in a loop, adding relaxation blocks, saturation pulses (calculated by B1 power and chemical shift), imaging pulses, delays, and ADC blocks.
Save the definitions to the .seq file using 'seq.set_definition' and 'seq.write(seq_fn)'.

steps.title: Prepare Subject for Imaging
steps.instruction: Set up the animal or human subject according to the scanner type.

substeps.instruction: For Rodents: Place in induction chamber with 4% wt/vol isoflurane; transfer to scan cradle and reduce isoflurane to 1–2% wt/vol via nose cone. Fix organ with bars/tape/cushions, apply lubricant eye ointment, and monitor respiration.
For Rodents: Maintain body temperature at 37°C using a hot air blower or water pump with a rectal sensor. Position cradle in RF coil with target organ at magnet center.

For Humans: Position subject on scanner bed and install organ-relevant coil. Verify ear-plugs and hand-pump communication. Position isocenter at the organ of interest using laser marking (subject must close eyes).

steps.title: Acquire MRI Data
steps.instruction: Perform the MRI scan and optional mapping sequences.

substeps.instruction: Acquire scout images and calibrate RF coils.
Determine slice location (axial recommended); use voxel size ~0.3 x 0.3 x 1 mm for rodents or 1.8 mm isotropic for humans.
Shim the magnetic field manually or automatically.
Scan using the chosen CEST-MRF pulse sequence.
Optional: Acquire T1, T2, B0, and/or B1 maps (e.g., using WASSR or WASABI sequences) using the same image geometry.
Optional: Acquire additional contrast-weighted images (T2-weighted, diffusion, perfusion, or traditional CEST Z-spectrum).

steps.title: Generate CEST-MRF Dictionary
steps.instruction: Simulate synthetic signal trajectories to create a dictionary (.mat file).

substeps.instruction: Define magnetic tissue properties in a 'configs.py' file and save them as a .yaml file using 'write_yaml_dict(cfg, yaml_fn)'.
Set water pool (T1, T2, f) and solute pool (e.g., Amine T1, T2, k, dw, f) parameters.
Run the simulation using 'generate_mrf_cest_dictionary' with the .seq and .yaml files as inputs.
Declare scanner limitations (max_grad, max_slew, rf_ringdown_time, etc.) for credible simulation.

steps.title: Perform Dot-Product Matching
steps.instruction: Quantify parameters by matching acquired data to the simulated dictionary.

substeps.instruction: Use the 'dot_prod_matching' function from the repository.
Reshape acquired data, perform L2 normalization on both dictionary and data, and calculate dot-products in batches (ensure image pixels are divisible by batch_size).
Identify the maximal dot-product for each batch to determine the corresponding parameter index.

steps.title: Train Supervised Reconstruction Network
steps.instruction: Train a fully connected neural network to reconstruct parameters from MRF signals.

substeps.instruction: Install PyTorch and OpenCV.
Define a network with three linear layers (input sig_n -> 300 -> 300 -> 2) and ReLU activations.
Import signals from the dictionary .mat file using a Pytorch Dataset class.
Set hyperparameters: learning_rate = 0.0001, batch_size = 256, num_epochs = 100, noise_std = 0.002.
Normalize output exchange parameters (concentration and proton exchange rate) to a range of -1 to 1 based on dictionary min/max values.
Train the network using the Adam optimizer and mean-squared-error loss.

steps.title: Perform Supervised Network Inference
steps.instruction: Use the trained network to reconstruct parameters from experimental data.

substeps.instruction: Load the trained model checkpoint into the network.
Load and reshape acquired data to (sig_n, pixels), then L2 normalize the data.
Transpose data and convert to a torch tensor.
Run inference in evaluation mode and un-normalize the output parameters back to physical units.

steps.title: Perform Sequential Reconstruction
steps.instruction: Train and run a network that uses both raw MRF signals and previously determined maps (e.g., T1, T2).

substeps.instruction: Normalize raw signals and previously determined water T1/T2 maps (range 0 to 1).
Concatenate the normalized maps with the noisy signals as input to the network.
Follow the training/inference pipeline similar to the supervised approach.

steps.title: Perform Multi-pool or Unsupervised Reconstruction
steps.instruction: Apply specialized reconstruction for human data or unsupervised learning.

substeps.instruction: For Multi-pool Human Data: Use the provided pre-trained network and inference code in the 'human_example' folder to reconstruct six parameter maps from 3T EPI data.
For Unsupervised Learning: Use real acquired data instead of dictionaries. Run the inference using 'python -m unsupervised_example.cnn_inference' with paths to data, results, and the trained model.

description: Figure 1. Fig. 1. Practical overview of the deep molecular magnetic resonance fingerprinting protocol . The workflow consists of three main stages: (1) Sample/subject preparation and acquisition protocol design. (2) Computational modeling and AI training, and (3) Evaluation and interpretation for the biological/clinical scenario of interest. Sub-figures in step (3) are reproduced with permission from Perlman et al. Nat. Biomed. Eng . 2022 29 , Weigand-Whittier et al., Magn. Res. Med . 2023 42 , and Perlman et al ., Magn. Res. Med . 2022 47 . Figure 2. Fig. 2. Experimental validation pipeline for CEST-MRF . Each column represents different biological settings, in an ascending order of complexity (left to right). ( Top ). Experimental stage. ( Center ). Expected CEST-MRF findings. ( Bottom ). Validation means. The histology sub-figure is reproduced with permission from Perlman et al. Nat. Biomed. Eng . 2022 29 . Figure 3. Fig. 3. A typical CEST MRF pulse sequence diagram. It consists of a frequency-selective saturation pulse train, a rapid read-out module (e.g., 3D EPI, turbo spin echo, etc.), recovery and delays. The sequence is repeated N times with varied saturation pulse parameters, yielding N raw MRF images. Figure 4. Fig. 4. Sequential learning of multi-proton-pool information . A semisolid MT-oriented MRF acquisition schedule yields raw images that are fed voxel-wise into the first NN, together with the quantitative water pool and field homogeneity maps (T 1 , T 2 , B 0 , B 1 ). This NN maps the semisolid MT pool exchange parameters, which are then fed, together with the previously obtained quantitative data, into the second NN, ultimately yielding the proton exchange parameters (f s and k sw ) of the compound of interest. Reproduced and modified with permission from Perlman et al ., NMR Biomed . 2023 84 . Figure 5. Fig. 5. Unsupervised-learning-based MRF reconstruction 40 .
